Between 1919 and 1929, all of the British Provinces, as well as most of the Princely states granted women the right to vote and, in some cases, allowed them to stand in local elections.

It also provided special quotas for women and ethnic groups in provincial legislatures. These provisions were incorporated into the Government of India Act 1935. Subsequent to which one of the following events, Gandhiji, who consistently
opposed untouchability and appealed for its eradication from all spheres,
decided to include the upliftment of 'Harijans' in his political and social
programme?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Arrest of Congress leadership at the time of the Quit India Movement

options.label: D
options.option_text: Promulgation of the Government of India Act, 1935

questions.solution_text:
The
Poona Pact of 1932
was a crucial agreement
between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar regarding the political
representation of the Depressed Classes (Dalits). Gandhiji strongly opposed the
British government's Communal Award, which proposed separate electorates for
Dalits. He believed it would divide Hindu society. To protest, Mahatma Gandhi
undertook a fast unto death while imprisoned in Yerwada Jail. The Poona Pact
was signed on 24 September 1932, ensuring reserved seats for Dalits within the
general electorate instead of separate electorates. Following this, Gandhiji
intensified his efforts for Harijan upliftment, founding the Harijan Sevak
Sangh to work for the eradication of untouchability.
